episode_title: Episode 201 - From Selling Cakes To Leading Bolt Food: Ivy Maingi on Bolt+, Couriers, & Kenya's Chicken Obsession!

real_qa.q: What is Bolt Plus and what are its pricing and key features?
real_qa.r: Bolt Plus is a subscription service launched by Bolt with a monthly fee of approximately 280 shillings. It introduced three new ways to book rides: priority booking, wait and save option, and ride by the hour. Bolt was recently ranked as one of the top 10 brands and the only mobility and delivery platform on the SuperBrands list.
real_qa.requete: Bolt Plus subscription price features Kenya

real_qa.q: How did Ivy Maingi transition from communications to running food delivery platforms?
real_qa.r: Ivy wanted to work at an ad agency initially, inspired by Mad Men, but realized she could combine storytelling with business. She had side businesses in college selling cupcakes and clothes from Gikomba with strategic positioning. Reading Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In inspired her to pursue tech roles, and when she applied for a position at Uber through LinkedIn, she was hired from Dubai and trained in SQL for three months before starting as an account manager.
real_qa.requete: Ivy Maingi career path communications food delivery

real_qa.q: What are the three main factors restaurants need from food delivery platforms?
real_qa.r: The first priority is driving sales to restaurants and merchants. The second is user experience and ease of the app—merchants need an intuitive platform where they can see all orders, customer complaints, and financial data. The third is unit economics: even with high sales, if commissions are too high or customers are overcharged, retention suffers. Additionally, robust support is critical since most merchants are new to platforms and many issues arise with courier deliveries.
real_qa.requete: what restaurants need food delivery platform

real_qa.q: What was the difference between Ivy's role as Commercial Manager versus General Manager at Glovo?
real_qa.r: As Commercial Manager, the focus was on content—getting all restaurants onto Glovo to maximize selection. As General Manager, the role became a generalist position focused on the entire customer journey: ensuring restaurants operate correctly and are available, that couriers deliver on time, and managing courier costs, which is the biggest line in the P&L. The shift meant couriers and logistics suddenly became core responsibilities overnight.
real_qa.requete: commercial manager vs general manager differences

real_qa.q: How does the QSR and delivery landscape differ between Kenya and Uganda?
real_qa.r: Kenya has multiple QSR brands including KFC, Symbisa brands, and Mixer, creating a developed quick-service restaurant ecosystem. Uganda, by contrast, has only one major QSR: KFC. This means the bulk of Ugandan partners are local, less tech-savvy businesses requiring support in Luganda. Additionally, Uganda has limited geography for expansion—while Kenya can expand to Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, and Eldoret, Ugandan expansion attempts to Jinja and Arua failed due to insufficient population and lack of QSRs.
real_qa.requete: Kenya Uganda QSR food delivery differences

guest.bio_context: Ivy Maingi joined Bolt Food Kenya in June 2026 with eight years of experience across East Africa's food delivery industry. She began at Uber Eats in Nairobi in December 2018, where she learned restaurant partnerships and account management. In 2023, she moved to Glovo as Commercial Manager for Food in Kenya, then became General Manager for Kenya before spending two years as Country Manager for Glovo Uganda, running the full market. Prior to delivery, she worked in brand and communications at Scannard, led institutional retail at Alibi Sharif & Sons, and started in corporate communications at John Gray Communications and Kenya Wildlife Service. She holds a degree from Daystar University in Communication and Media Studies.
